sentences.text: Revenue went from essentially nil in FY2019 [F1] to $5,387 million in FY2025 [F7], a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [D342].
The step change was FY2022, when revenue jumped 2914.5% to $1,658 million [D83][F4] on deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [P67], then grew 167.4% in FY2023 [D135].
Growth then decelerated sharply to 12.1% in FY2024 [D187] and 8.4% in FY2025 [D239].
The loss narrowed every year after FY2022: operating loss fell from $6,856 million [F23] to $3,585 million [F26], lifting operating margin from -413.5% [F28] to -66.5% [F31].
In FY2025 Software and Services contributed +21.6pp of the 8.4% revenue growth [D295][D239], while New electric vehicles subtracted 10.5pp [D288].

Software and services revenue rose 221.7% to $1,557 million [D294][S14], primarily on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture, remarketing and repair and maintenance [P18].
That segment reached 28.9% of revenue [D321], while Automotive fell 14.6% [D315] to 71.1% of revenue [D314].
Automotive revenue fell as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles, partly from expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 [P22].
Operating costs grew 6.9% against 8.4% revenue growth [D258][D239], an incremental operating margin of 264.7% [D265].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7% in FY2025 [F19], against a window median of -45.8% [D332] and a FY2021 low of -845.5% [D330].
Operating margin of -66.5% [F31] remains far below the -129.4% window median [D326] in absolute terms but is the window high [D325].
The FY2025 bridge was almost entirely cost of revenue, +26.8pp [D267], with R&D +1.5pp [D268] and SG&A -0.5pp [D269].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0% [D255] as Automotive cost of revenues dropped on fewer vehicles produced and lower raw material, component and conversion costs [P21].
SG&A rose 9.9% [D257] on expanding go-to-market operations, higher payroll and stock-based compensation [P13].
Operating cash flow was -$779 million in FY2025 [F64], a -14.5% margin [D227], against a -132.9% window median free-cash-flow margin [D335].
The improvement in operating cash use was primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Free cash flow was -$2,489 million [F78], a -46.2% margin [D226], with capex of $1,710 million [F71] at 31.7% of revenue [D225] and 2.18x D&A [D228].
Capex rose 49.9% [D246] on expansion of production capacity at the Normal Factory and next-generation platforms [P3].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million in FY2025 [D231] from $3,259 million [D179], as cash and investments dropped 21.0% [D261].
Net cash is still 30.5% of revenue [D232], above the 17.8% autos peer median (n=4) [D352] at the 75th percentile [D351].
Financing inflow of $886 million [F92] came primarily from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group on the Financial Milestone [P2].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% [D260] to 1,186 million [X91], so EPS improved 34.5% [D242] while net loss fell 23.2% [D241].
Net losses persist in all seven years, from -$426 million in FY2019 [F32] to -$3,646 million in FY2025 [F38] [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D223] and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2], equal to 20.7% of the operating loss [D237].
Cash and investments of $6,082 million [D229] cover 2.4 years of the latest burn [D236] [R3].
New electric vehicles were 67.6% of revenue [D286] and fell 12.5% [D287] [R4], and Automotive fell 14.6% [D315] [R5].
Product revenue members sum to 129% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they cannot be added [R6].
Gross margin: a move above the FY2025 level of 2.7% [F19] would confirm the cost trend; a slip back below zero would reverse it, visible in the FY2026 10-K.
Operating margin: holding above the -66.5% window high [D325] confirms the narrowing loss; falling back toward the -129.4% median [D326] would reverse it.
Net cash: staying above the FY2025 $1,642 million [D231] confirms the balance sheet holds; a drop below the 2.4 years of burn coverage [D236] would tighten liquidity.
